PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 10/31/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Continued cough and persistent fatigue despite recent antibiotic therapy.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit one week after initiating a course of Azithromycin for his exacerbated COPD symptoms. He reports minimal improvement in his cough, which remains productive with yellow sputum. The fatigue persists, and he feels that his overall endurance has not improved. He notes that while his wheezing has slightly decreased, he still experiences shortness of breath during activities of daily living, particularly when climbing stairs. He denies any fever, chills, or hemoptysis since the last visit.
Mr. Fairfax has been adhering to the prescribed antibiotic regimen and continues to utilize nebulized albuterol every hour as needed. He reports that he has been diligent in maintaining his symptom diary, noting the frequency of his cough and sputum characteristics, which have remained consistent.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + productive cough with yellow sputum, + mild wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/76 mmHg - Heart Rate: 80 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 24 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 90% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued but is alert and in no acute distress.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Mild wheezing noted on auscultation; increased bronchial breath sounds; moderate expiratory wheezing with prolonged expiration; rhonchi heard bilaterally.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with persistent exacerbation; ongoing productive cough and fatigue suggest inadequate response to current treatment. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload. 3. Persistent fatigue likely multifactorial, exacerbated by respiratory symptoms and underlying cardiac condition.
PLAN
1. Extend antibiotic therapy for an additional 7 days with Azithromycin 500 mg daily, considering the slow response to treatment and the presence of yellow sputum. 2. Initiate a course of oral Prednisone 20 mg daily for 5 days to help reduce inflammation associated with COPD exacerbation. 3. Continue nebulized albuterol every hour as needed; discuss the addition of a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) and a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) to optimize management at the next visit. 4. Continue oral furosemide 40 mg daily; monitor renal function and electrolytes closely in light of ongoing symptoms. 5. Schedule follow-up in one week for re-evaluation of respiratory status, sputum characteristics, and fatigue levels. Consider pulmonary function testing if symptoms do not improve.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with a revised prescription for oral Azithromycin and a new prescription for oral Prednisone. He was advised to continue using nebulized albuterol as needed and to maintain his symptom diary. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for one week from today to reassess his response to the adjusted treatment plan and further optimize his management.
